What Apple earns
after the hardware sale

The devices still lead the story. But a closer look at Apple’s sales and costs shows why Services deserve a bigger headline.

THE SHORT VERSION

A smaller slice of sales. A larger slice of gross profit.

In fiscal 2025, Apple reported $109.2 billion in Services net sales. That was 26.2% of total net sales. Subtract the reported Services cost of sales, and Services contributed $82.3 billion in gross profit—42.2% of Apple’s total gross profit.

An iPhone, Mac, or Watch is easy to see. The revenue attached to a device over time is harder to picture. Apple’s financial statements draw a useful line between Products and Services, and the distance between those lines has become an important part of the company’s story.

Products still account for most of the business: $307.0 billion of Apple’s $416.2 billion in fiscal 2025 net sales. Services contributed the remaining $109.2 billion. The sales mix alone is striking; the cost figures make it more revealing.

01 / THE SALES MIX

The share has been moving

In fiscal 2021, Services represented 18.7% of Apple’s net sales. By fiscal 2025, the share was 26.2%, a gain of 7.5 percentage points. These figures compare reported annual sales, not the value of a single customer or device.

That direction matters because the two categories carry different reported costs. Revenue tells us how large each business is; gross profit reveals a second dimension.

02 / FOLLOW THE GROSS PROFIT

Services punch above their sales share

For fiscal 2025, Apple reported $26.8 billion in cost of sales against $109.2 billion of Services net sales. The difference is $82.3 billion in gross profit. Products generated $112.9 billion in gross profit from $307.0 billion in sales. This is gross profit before research, marketing, and other operating expenses.

THE TAKEAWAY

Services made up about one quarter of net sales, but more than two fifths of gross profit.

That is a comparison of accounting categories, not a claim that each service has the same margin. Apple does not give a product-by-product profit breakdown here, and gross profit should not be confused with net income.

03 / BEHIND THE CATEGORY

What Apple calls “Services”

Apple groups several businesses under the Services heading. Its fiscal 2025 filing describes advertising, AppleCare, cloud services, digital content and subscriptions, the App Store, and payment services. The report gives a combined Services figure; it does not disclose a separate sales total for every item in this list.

That distinction is useful for readers. A fast-growing category can contain very different customer behaviors and economics. The published numbers show the category’s scale and gross profit, while leaving some of the internal mix out of view.

04 / COMMON QUESTIONS

The details, clarified.

Does Services mean subscriptions only?

No. Apple’s category also includes advertising, AppleCare, the App Store, cloud services, and payment services. It reports their combined revenue.

Is gross profit the same as net income?

No. Gross profit is net sales less cost of sales. Research and development, selling and administrative expenses, taxes, and other items affect the final net-income figure.

Does Apple disclose the profit of every service?

Not in this breakdown. The filing reports combined Services net sales and cost of sales, so this chart cannot show the profitability of each individual service.

SOURCES & METHOD

How we calculated the chart

All FY2025 figures come from Apple’s FY2025 Form 10-K, in U.S. dollars. We subtracted cost of sales from net sales in each category and divided each category by the reported total. The FY2021 comparison comes from Apple’s FY2023 Form 10-K, which includes FY2021 data. Dollar amounts in prose are rounded to one decimal billion; the calculations use the filing’s millions.
